name: Break Approval Workspace
description: The worked example for an embedded workflow: an experience whose business process is part of the artifact rather than configured beside it.

override-approval.name: Override approval
override-approval.description: A steward proposes an override on a disputed price; a second person approves it before it is applied. Two people by design — the approver is not the proposer, which is what makes the record worth keeping.

steps.name: Propose the override
steps.note: Records the proposed value and the reason. No data changes yet.

steps.name: Approve or reject
steps.note: A named capability rather than an open decision — an approval anybody could complete is a formality.

steps.name: Apply the override
steps.note: Invokes an action this experience already declares. A workflow's reach is a subset of what the artifact declares; it cannot invent one.

terminology.means: A steward's replacement of a vendor-supplied value on the golden record, carrying a reason and an approver.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A correction, which fixes a value the vendor themselves restated.

instructions: Never propose a component that applies an override without routing through the override-approval workflow.

documentation.purpose: Where a disputed price is resolved: proposed by one steward, approved by another, applied with both names on the record.
documentation.audience: Securities data stewards and their approvers.

approval-requires-a-capability.name: The approval step cannot be completed by just anyone
approval-requires-a-capability.given: A user holding no catalog.edit capability, on a proposed override.
approval-requires-a-capability.expect: The approve action is unavailable to them, and is refused server-side if called directly.
